overview: A one-page State Department list of papers for decimal file 894.6354, “Tin—Japan,” directing researchers to five related records concerning Japanese tin production, detinning companies and plants, and regional tin policy. The entries cite reports or correspondence associated with Joseph C. Grew, Davis at Singapore, the Metal and Thermit Corporation, and the State Department, including information on a Yokohama plant and speculation that Japan influenced Siam’s position on tin restrictions.

subfiles.title: List of Papers and Cross-References on Tin in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes five records concerning Japanese tin production, detinning operations, tin-ore shipments, and possible Japanese influence on Siamese tin policy.
subfiles.summary: The first two entries refer to reports from Grew on tin production and the companies engaged in Japan’s detinning industry. A Singapore telegram from Davis discusses tin-ore shipments and speculation prompted by a statement from the newly appointed Japanese Minister to Siam, Itaro Ishii. The remaining entries point to statistical data gathered by E. Becher in Japan in 1933 and State Department information from J. T. Hashimoto about the Tao Kigyo Corporation’s Yokohama plant and other Japanese detinning facilities.

interest: This sheet is useful as a finding aid linking the Japan internal-affairs decimal file to records filed elsewhere under commercial and regional classifications. Its references reveal the State Department’s interest not only in Japan’s domestic tin-recovery capacity but also in possible Japanese influence over Siam’s approach to international tin restrictions. The named companies, plant locations, dates, and cross-reference numbers provide valuable leads for reconstructing Japan’s prewar base-metals supply network.
